title: The Determinant: How Much a Matrix Stretches Space
logline: Watch a grid warp, follow one square, and the determinant becomes a number you can see.
color_story: PRIMARY blue is the moving grid; POSITIVE green is i-hat and NEGATIVE red is j-hat (the classic basis colours); HIGHLIGHT yellow is the unit square; SECONDARY teal is other regions; ACCENT terracotta is the determinant itself; FAINT grey is the original grid left behind.

scenes.title: A matrix moves the plane
scenes.purpose: Picture a 2x2 matrix as a transformation of the whole plane.

beats.narration: What does the determinant of a matrix actually measure? Not a formula to memorise, but a number you can see.
beats.visual: Title card 'The Determinant' with italic subtitle 'how much a matrix stretches space'.

beats.narration: Think of a two by two matrix as a machine that moves every point of the plane. These two arrows mark one step right, and one step up.
beats.visual: Clear. A faint static grid and a blue grid on top fill the frame; green i-hat and red j-hat arrows grow from the origin.

beats.narration: Apply the matrix, and the whole grid moves with it. Lines stay straight and evenly spaced, and the arrows land on the matrix's two columns.
beats.visual: The matrix [[2, 1], [0, 1.5]] appears top right on a dark plate, columns tinted green and red; the blue grid and both arrows transform, i-hat to (2, 0) and j-hat to (1, 1.5).

scenes.title: Follow one square
scenes.purpose: Find the factor by which the unit square's area changes.

beats.narration: Now watch a single square, sitting on the two arrows, one unit on each side. Its area is exactly one.
beats.visual: Heading. Untransformed grid and arrows; a yellow unit square fills in on top of them; readout 'area = 1' top right on a plate.

beats.narration: After the transformation, it becomes a parallelogram. Measure it, and its area is three.
beats.visual: The grid, arrows and square transform together; the square becomes a parallelogram; the readout changes to 'area = 3'.

beats.narration: That stretching factor, three, is the determinant. It tells you how much the matrix scales area.
beats.visual: Below the readout, 'det = 3' is written with the 3 in terracotta and boxed; the parallelogram pulses once.

scenes.title: Every area, the same factor
scenes.purpose: Show that all regions scale by the determinant, not only the square.

beats.narration: The surprising part is that every region grows by that same factor, whatever its shape.
beats.visual: Heading. Grid with a teal circle, a teal triangle and a small teal square scattered near the origin.

beats.narration: Every shape can be filled with tiny grid squares, and every one of those grows by exactly three. So the whole shape does too.
beats.visual: The grid and all three shapes transform; each shape gets a small 'times 3' label.

scenes.title: Zero and negative
scenes.purpose: Connect the formula to the picture and read the special cases.

beats.narration: For a matrix with entries a, b, c and d, the determinant is a times d, minus b times c. Here that's two times one and a half, minus zero: three.
beats.visual: Heading. Centered on a plate, det [[a, b], [c, d]] = ad - bc is written; below it the numbers: det [[2, 1], [0, 1.5]] = 2 times 1.5 minus 1 times 0 = 3, with 3 in terracotta.

beats.narration: If the determinant is zero, the plane is squashed onto a single line, and every area collapses to nothing.
beats.visual: Clear the formulas. Grid, arrows and yellow square; the matrix [[1, 2], [0.5, 1]] collapses everything onto a line; readout 'det = 0'. Then the grid restores.

beats.narration: And a negative determinant means space has been flipped over, like turning a sheet of paper, while its size still measures the stretch.
beats.visual: The matrix [[1, 0.5], [0, -1]] flips the grid: j-hat now points down and the square flips below the axis; readout 'det = -1' with 'orientation flipped'.
